Title: MIN-6: All core authentication paths work on web and mobile
Preconditions: A test account exists; the web app and the mobile app are installed
Steps:
1. On the web app, complete sign-up, login, logout and password reset
2. Repeat the same four flows on the mobile app
Expected Result: Each of the four flows completes successfully on both web and mobile

Title: MIN-6: Passwords are stored encrypted with bcrypt
Preconditions: Database read access to a test environment; a test account was just created
Steps:
1. Create an account with the password 'Test@1234'
2. Read the stored password value for that account in the database
Expected Result: The stored value is a bcrypt hash (starts with $2a$, $2b$ or $2y$), not the plain password

Title: MIN-6: Session token is a valid JWT
Steps:
1. Log in and capture the session token
2. Decode the token header and payload
Expected Result: The token is a signed JWT with an expiry claim and a user identifier, and it carries no password or secret data

Title: MIN-6: Tampered or expired JWT is rejected
Preconditions: A valid JWT has been captured after login
Steps:
1. Change one character in the token payload and call a protected API
2. Call the same API with an expired token
Expected Result: Both requests are rejected with an unauthorized response and no user data is returned

Title: MIN-6: Profile changes sync between database and frontend
Preconditions: User is logged in on two browsers
Steps:
1. In browser 1 edit the display name and save
2. Check the stored profile record in the database
3. Reload the profile page in browser 2
Expected Result: The new name is saved in the database and shows in both browsers

Title: MIN-6: Failed profile save leaves data consistent
Preconditions: User is logged in; the profile save call can be made to fail (for example by blocking it in dev tools)
Steps:
1. Edit the display name
2. Block the save request and click Save
3. Reload the page
Expected Result: An error message is shown, and the database and the frontend still show the old name

Title: MIN-6: Authentication pages adapt to web and mobile screen sizes
Preconditions: Sign-up, login and reset pages are reachable
Steps:
1. Open each page at 1440 px width
2. Open each page at 375 px width
Expected Result: Content fits the width, there is no horizontal scroll, and all fields and buttons are usable at both sizes

Title: MIN-7: Sign up with a unique email and a strong password
Preconditions: The email test1@example.com is not registered; the sign-up page is open
Steps:
1. Enter test1@example.com
2. Enter the password 'Secure@123'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The account is created and a verification email is sent to test1@example.com

Title: MIN-7: Password of exactly 8 characters is accepted
Preconditions: The sign-up page is open; the email test2@example.com is not registered
Steps:
1. Enter test2@example.com
2. Enter the 8-character password 'abcdef1!'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The account is created, because 8 characters with 1 number and 1 special character meets the rule

Title: MIN-7: Duplicate email is rejected with the stated message
Steps:
1. Enter test1@example.com
2. Enter the password 'Secure@123'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The message 'Email already registered.' is shown and no second account is created

Title: MIN-7: Password shorter than 8 characters is rejected
Steps:
1. Enter an unused email
2. Enter the 7-character password 'abcde1!'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The password is rejected with a message about the rules and no account is created

Title: MIN-7: Password without a number is rejected
Steps:
1. Enter an unused email
2. Enter the password 'Password!'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The password is rejected with a message about the rules and no account is created

Title: MIN-7: Password without a special character is rejected
Steps:
1. Enter an unused email
2. Enter the password 'Password1'
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: The password is rejected with a message about the rules and no account is created

Title: MIN-7: Invalid email format is rejected
Steps:
1. Enter 'user@@example' as the email
2. Enter a strong password
3. Click Submit
Expected Result: A validation error is shown on the email field and no account is created

Title: MIN-7: Submit with empty fields
Steps:
1. Leave the email and password empty
2. Click Submit
Expected Result: Required-field messages are shown and no account is created

Title: MIN-7: Duplicate-email message is clearly visible
Steps:
1. Submit the sign-up form with test1@example.com
2. Look at where the message appears
Expected Result: 'Email already registered.' appears next to the form, is readable, and is not hidden by other content

Title: MIN-7: Password is never exposed in the request URL or response
Preconditions: Browser developer tools network tab is open
Steps:
1. Submit a valid sign-up form
2. Inspect the request URL, request body and response
Expected Result: The password is sent only in the request body over HTTPS and is not in the URL or echoed in the response

Title: MIN-7: Sign-up fields reject script injection
Steps:
1. Enter <script>alert(1)</script> in the email field
2. Submit the form
Expected Result: The input is rejected or escaped, no script runs, and nothing unsafe is stored

Title: MIN-7: Registration endpoint creates an account
Preconditions: The registration endpoint is reachable; the email is unused
Steps:
1. Send a registration request with a unique email and a strong password
2. Read the response
Expected Result: The API returns a success status and the account exists

Title: MIN-7: Registration endpoint rejects a duplicate email
Steps: 1. Send a registration request with test1@example.com
Expected Result: The API returns an error status and the body contains the message 'Email already registered.'

Title: MIN-8: Login with valid credentials
Steps:
1. Open the login page
2. Enter the valid email and password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: The user is redirected to the main dashboard and a secure JWT session is started

Title: MIN-8: Logout destroys the session
Preconditions: User is logged in and on the dashboard
Steps:
1. Click Logout
2. Observe the page
Expected Result: The session token is destroyed and the user is redirected to the public landing page

Title: MIN-8: Wrong password shows the stated message and keeps the inputs
Steps:
1. Enter the valid email
2. Enter a wrong password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: The message 'Invalid username or password' is shown and the entered values stay in the fields

Title: MIN-8: Unknown user shows the same message
Steps:
1. Enter an email that is not registered
2. Enter any password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: The message 'Invalid username or password' is shown, the same as for a wrong password

Title: MIN-8: Login with empty fields
Steps:
1. Leave both fields empty
2. Click Login
Expected Result: A required-field message is shown and no session is created

Title: MIN-8: Old token is rejected after logout
Preconditions: User is logged in; the JWT has been captured
Steps:
1. Click Logout
2. Call a protected API with the captured token
Expected Result: The API rejects the request as unauthorized

Title: MIN-8: Back button after logout does not show the dashboard
Preconditions: User is logged in and on the dashboard
Steps:
1. Click Logout
2. Click the browser Back button
Expected Result: The dashboard content is not shown; the user stays on the landing page or the login page

Title: MIN-8: Dashboard cannot be opened without logging in
Steps: 1. Open the dashboard URL directly
Expected Result: The user is redirected to the login page and no dashboard data is shown

Title: MIN-8: Login resists SQL injection
Steps:
1. Enter "' OR '1'='1" as the email
2. Enter any password
3. Click Login
Expected Result: Login fails with 'Invalid username or password' and no session is created

Title: MIN-8: Session token is stored and sent securely
Preconditions: User is logged in; browser developer tools are open
Steps:
1. Inspect where the token is stored
2. Inspect how it is sent with requests
Expected Result: The token is sent only over HTTPS and is not readable by page scripts (for example an HttpOnly cookie), as the team's standard requires

Title: MIN-8: Login endpoint returns a token for valid credentials
Steps:
1. Send a login request with valid credentials
2. Read the response
Expected Result: The API returns a success status and a JWT

Title: MIN-8: Login endpoint rejects invalid credentials
Steps: 1. Send a login request with a wrong password
Expected Result: The API returns an unauthorized status and no token

Title: MIN-9: Reset email is sent for a registered address
Preconditions: A registered user exists; the reset page is open
Steps:
1. Enter the registered email
2. Submit the request
3. Open the inbox
Expected Result: An email with a reset link arrives

Title: MIN-9: Set a new password with a valid link
Preconditions: A reset email was received less than 15 minutes ago
Steps:
1. Click the link in the email
2. Enter a new strong password
3. Submit
4. Log in with the new password
Expected Result: The password is changed and login with the new password succeeds

Title: MIN-9: Link works just before 15 minutes
Preconditions: A reset email was received 14 minutes ago
Steps: 1. Click the link in the email
Expected Result: The reset form opens normally

Title: MIN-9: Expired link shows the stated message and a button
Preconditions: A reset email was received more than 15 minutes ago
Steps: 1. Click the link in the email
Expected Result: The message 'Link has expired' is shown with a button to request a new link

Title: MIN-9: Request a new link from the expired page
Steps:
1. Click the button to request a new link
2. Open the inbox
3. Click the new link
Expected Result: A new email arrives and its link opens the reset form

Title: MIN-9: Link can be used only once
Preconditions: A reset link was already used to change the password
Steps: 1. Click the same link again
Expected Result: The link is rejected and the password cannot be reset with it

Title: MIN-9: Invalid email format on the reset page
Steps:
1. Enter 'user@@example'
2. Submit the request
Expected Result: A validation error is shown and no email is sent

Title: MIN-9: Reset request for an unregistered email
Preconditions: The reset page is open; the email is not registered
Steps:
1. Enter an email that is not registered
2. Submit the request
Expected Result: No reset email is sent and the page does not reveal whether the email exists (assumed; the ticket does not say)

Title: MIN-9: Weak new password is rejected
Preconditions: A valid reset link is open
Steps:
1. Enter the new password 'abc'
2. Submit
Expected Result: The password is rejected with a message about the rules (assumed to match the sign-up rules)

Title: MIN-9: Reset links are unique and unpredictable
Steps:
1. Request two reset links for the same account
2. Compare the two tokens
Expected Result: The tokens are different and show no sequence or pattern

Title: MIN-9: Tampered reset token is rejected
Preconditions: A valid reset link is available
Steps:
1. Change one character in the token part of the link
2. Open the link
Expected Result: The link is rejected and no password change is possible

Title: MIN-9: Expired-link page is clear and usable
Steps:
1. Look at the page
2. Tab to the new-link button and press Enter
Expected Result: The message is readable, the button is visible and reachable by keyboard, and it starts a new request

Title: MIN-9: Token validation rejects an expired token
Steps: 1. Send the expired token to the reset-token validation endpoint
Expected Result: The API returns an error status that identifies the token as expired
